subject: Audit & Access Logs — export slices, retention windows, and TTL/hold options
messages:

Subject: Question: audit/access log retention & export formats for regulator

Hi Ben,

We are preparing for a regulatory audit in Q3 and need to confirm a couple of things about Redwood-hosted audit and access logs for the environment running our production tenant: GreenBridge-FIN. Specifically:  

- What is the default retention window for access logs and audit trails in the hosted Redwood service? Do you differentiate between "access logs" (API auth, token activity) and "audit trails" (resource changes, admin actions)?
- Can we export historical logs on demand? If so, what formats are available (CSV/JSON/syslog) and what is the lead time/SLA for a bulk export?
- Are there options for longer-term retention (eg. 7 years) for regulated records, and what deployment types support that (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)?
- Is there a documented deletion/TTL process (how records are purged) and a way to put a legal hold to prevent deletion while an audit is underway?

If you can send a short write-up or point me to the page and any export schema, that would be great. We may need an evidence bundle for the audit team (log samples + retention statement).

Thanks,
Marina Lowe
Director, Compliance
GreenBridge Financial

Hi Marina — apologies for the longer reply, below is an operational summary and the artifacts attached. I kept the answers short and included the actionable steps to request exports.

Summary (short)
- "Access logs": authentication, token exchange, and API call metadata. Default hosted retention: 90 days.
- "Audit trails": configuration changes, role/permission changes, resource lifecycle events. Default hosted retention: 365 days (we retain audit-level change events longer by default).
- Exports: Supported formats — JSONL (line-delimited JSON), CSV (schema attached), and syslog (RFC5424) for live forwarding to your collector.
- Bulk export SLA: For hosted tenants we generally schedule bulk historical exports within 72 hours; export throughput depends on time range and token volume. For Dedicated/Private we typically provide expedited exports (24–48 hours) and can set up continuous offsite archiving if required.
- Long-term retention: Supported on Dedicated and Private deployments. We can provision archival retention profiles (1/3/5/7 years) and integrate with customer S3 buckets or on-prem archival targets. Hosted customers can purchase extended retention as an add-on (multi-month contracts) but there are some technical and cost limits — we'll propose options for GreenBridge.
- Deletion/TTL & legal hold: Logs are subject to configurable TTL policies. Deletion is automated by TTL unless a legal hold is applied. Legal hold is an administrative flag tied to the tenant that prevents any automated purge; we keep that in our control plane audit and surface it to customer admins. For Private, legal hold is enforced via customer-controlled retention settings.

Operational notes (how to request an export)
1) File a request through our portal (Support > Audit Export) or via your TAM (Ben). Include time range, desired format (JSONL/CSV/syslog), and delivery target (S3/HTTP stream).
2) For >12 months of data we will do a scoped run and estimate export size; expect a lead time of 48–72 hours on Hosted.
3) Delivery options: one-time downloadable archive (GZIP), one-time push to your S3, or continuous push to your syslog/collectors.
4) We redact sensitive PII fields by default in hosted exports unless a Data Processing Addendum and explicit allowed fields are configured; Private/Dedicated can deliver raw audit events per contract.

Export schema (high level)
- Attached CSV shows column layout (timestamp, tenant_id, event_type, actor_id, source_ip, resource, action, success, metadata_json).
- JSONL includes the same fields with metadata as nested JSON; sample in the attachment.

Retention matrix (attached)
- redwood_audit_retention_matrix.pdf: shows default windows by deployment type, options for extensions, and associated costs.

CLI example (for Dedicated/Private customers with redwoodctl access):
$ redwoodctl logs export --tenant GreenBridge-FIN --from 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z --to 2024-12-31T23:59:59Z --format jsonl --target s3://greenbridge-audit-exports/2023-2024/ --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/abcd

Evidence note for auditors
- We can produce a short signed statement describing retention windows, legal hold capability, export formats, and delivery chain. We can also bundle a 24–48 hour sample extract (scrubbed to remove PII) and a manifest (checksums) for chain-of-custody.

Attached: redwood_audit_retention_matrix.pdf; audit_log_export_schema.csv

If you want, Ben or I can hop on a 30-min call to walk the audit team through the attachments and the export process — we find it helps speed sign-off.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
